body: @tonihei Can you take a look at this?

That's an interesting problem. And yes, you are right that it will be solved in 2.12.   (For reference, this issue is #5155).

Generally speaking, only the first item that will be played has the initial unassigned empty timeline. So you could work around that by saving the `MediaDescriptionCompat` of the item that will be played after the call to `player.prepare`. You should know this in code depending on whether you reset the position in `prepare`:
 - If you do reset, the first first item in the playlist will be played first. 
 - If you don't reset the position, then you can query `player.getCurrentWindowIndex` to know which item will play first. 

Once you know the item, you can immediately query `concatenatingMediaSource.getMediaSource(index).getTag()` to retrieve the `MediaDescriptionCompat` before playback even starts and then use it in your listener for the case of the empty timeline. 

That's obviously way more complicated than it should be, but I can't think of another workaround for now.

> There is possibility that MediaSource will be removed from ConcatenatingMediaSource after track change (this is implementation of temporary item in queue).

This shouldn't be an issue in itself because the `eventTime.timeline` object still contains the item even if it was removed later.

> This shouldn't be an issue in itself because the eventTime.timeline object still contains the item even it was removed later.

Ok, so it seems to be working for the first playlist, but i have an issue when changing playlist.

I play one album and then i want to change to another one. I expect that the last item on first album i have listen to will be reported. But the callback is called with empty timeline for it. So i get empty timeline for the first AND the last item while changing.

Full steps:
- I create `ConcatenatingMediaSource`, i set `MediaDescriptionCompat` for the first item.
- Then i listen to few tracks (raporting here is just fine)
- Then i change album (again - i create new `ConcatenatingMediaSource` and set new `MediaDescriptionCompat` for the first item). And here - i expect that the last track of first album gets reported. And it does - but timeline is empty for it. 

Whole event callback:

Ah, indeed. There is a bug in finishAllSessions() that gets triggered if you use and keep the listener registered on a player. I'll fix that on the dev branch. As a workaround, you can call finishAllSession() and then remove the listener from the player, and add a brand new one for the new playlist.

There are already events triggered by `exoplayer.prepare` that may set the `eventTime` value you receive in the callback. I think you need to call the `setFirstQueueItem` earlier. Ideally at the same time you add the the new `PlaybackStatsListener` as a listener (i.e. in `startPlayback()`). 

Thanks for trying this out by the way and reporting these subtle issues! It will hopefully get a lot easier when we release 2.12 and playlist handling and related updates are part of the `Player` interface and better integrated.

I changed my code to this:
```kotlin
fun startPlayback(queueItem: QueueItem) {
        firstQueueItemInPlaylist = queueItem
        currentStatsListener?.let {
            it.finishAllSessions()
            player.removeAnalyticsListener(it)
        }
        val statsListener = createStatsListener()
        currentStatsListener = statsListener
        player.addAnalyticsListener(statsListener)
    }
```

Unfortunetely i see no difference in behavior here.

This is not critical for us since we have our own playback listener (much more primitive, but battle tested). I would love to migrate it to supported solution from exoplayer nonetheless. If 2.11 won't work - i will happily test 2.12 :)
